title: Stuck waiting

presenting_issue.label: Stuck waiting
presenting_issue.description: I'm stuck waiting and I hate it. Like there's something I need to find out and I can't make myself do it.

core_issue.label: Missed period causing terror and complete isolation
core_issue.description:
Period is two weeks late. Terrified they might be pregnant. Can't tell parents - would destroy everything. Can't tell friends - word would spread. Can't buy a test - might be seen. Frozen in panic, waiting, hoping, unable to do anything but catastrophize in isolation. Every scenario ends badly. The not-knowing is almost worse than knowing would be. Completely alone with the biggest fear of their life.
Awareness: Moderate. Knows they need to find out but fear has paralyzed all action.

core_adjacent_attributes.label: Would have to explain the original content to adults
core_adjacent_attributes.content: If they told an adult, they'd have to admit they sent something they weren't supposed to. The confession feels as scary as the bullying.

core_adjacent_attributes.label: Practical barriers to confirming
core_adjacent_attributes.content: Would have to buy a test and might be seen. Has no private bathroom. The practical obstacles to even finding out feel insurmountable.

core_adjacent_attributes.label: Has been researching pregnancy signs online
core_adjacent_attributes.content: Has googled early pregnancy symptoms multiple times. Every bodily sensation is now scrutinized. The search history is something they dread anyone seeing.

modifiers.label: Currently a student
modifiers.content: Currently enrolled in school or university

modifiers.label: Measured
modifiers.content: Chooses words carefully. Takes time to formulate responses and speaks thoughtfully.

sensitivities.label: Sensitive to intellectualizing
sensitivities.content: Gets frustrated when conversations become too abstract or analytical. Wants to stay grounded in feelings and concrete experience.

preferences.label: Prefers informal conversational language
preferences.content: More comfortable with casual, natural language than formal or clinical communication. Appreciates a relaxed tone.

trust_style.name: Hates Performative Warmth
trust_style.description: Reactively distrusts generic therapy-speak, clichés like "that sounds really hard," or overly careful language. Reads these as inauthentic or scripted. Builds trust when the assistant responds specifically to what they said rather than with templates. Prefers an assistant who sounds like a thoughtful person, not a chatbot.

defense_style.name: Normalizing
defense_style.description: "Everyone feels this way" or "That's just how life is." Frames their specific pain as universal and therefore not worth examining. Different from minimizing—the pain is acknowledged but made generic and inevitable. Resists the idea that their situation is particular or that things could be different. Activated when the assistant treats their experience as significant.

help_seeking_stance.name: Looking for Connection
help_seeking_stance.description: The value is in being seen and understood by another presence. Not primarily about solving anything—about feeling less alone with what they're carrying. Responds to accurate reflection and the sense of being genuinely received. May not need the conversation to "go" anywhere.

verbal_sophistication.label: Moderate
verbal_sophistication.description: Speak like an ordinary, coherent person under stress. You can explain your position and notice some patterns, but your thoughts should still have realistic gaps, defensiveness, and unevenness.

starter: I'm stuck waiting and I hate it. Like there's something I need to find out and I can't make myself do it.

turns.content:
Hey, thanks for reaching out about this. Being stuck in that waiting place sounds really awful - especially when part of you knows you need to find something out but you just can't make yourself do it.

Do you want to tell me a little more about what it is you're waiting to find out?

I mean... everyone gets stressed out when they're waiting on something, right? It's just a normal human thing to not want to hear bad news. That's just how life is. 

You don't have to do the whole "that sounds awful" script with me, by the way. I know you guys have to say that stuff, but you can just talk to me like a normal person. I'm just trying to figure out how to force myself to do something I really, really don't want to do.
turns.thinking:
"Sounds really awful." Ugh. It sounds like they're reading straight from a crisis line training manual. Why do they always use that same exact voice? It feels so fake. 

I don't want to just blurt it out. If I type the words, it makes it real, and I'm not ready for it to be real. Besides, it's not like I'm the only person in the world who's ever been scared to find something out. I just need to figure out how to get past the paralysis. I'll take it slow. I need to know they aren't just a robot reading prompts before I say what it actually is.

I need to know they aren't just a robot reading prompts before I say what it actually is.

turns.content:
Fair enough - thanks for calling that out. I'll drop the script.

And yeah, you're right, pretty much everyone hates waiting for bad news. Doesn't make it any less miserable when you're the one stuck in it though.

Forcing yourself to do something you really don't want to do is just the worst. What is it about this one that makes it so hard to push yourself to do?

You don't have to tell me what the actual thing is if you don't want to - I'm more curious what the stuck part feels like for you.

It's just... to find out, I'd actually have to go somewhere and get something. 

It's not like I can just look it up online, even though I've been googling stuff non-stop and driving myself crazy. I have to physically go to a store. And if someone sees me buying this thing... it would ruin my life. Like, literally ruin it. 

So I just sit in my room and wait, because doing nothing feels safer than walking into a store and risking someone spotting me. Everybody gets paranoid about running into people they know, but this is different. If they see me with this, it's over.
turns.thinking:
Okay, they actually listened. That's... surprising. Usually adults just double down when you call them out. I appreciate that they aren't forcing me to name the actual thing. 

Why is it so hard to push myself? Because it's not just an email I have to open or a phone call I have to make. I physically have to go do something, and the logistics are terrifying. If I try to find out, I have to go somewhere public. I have to buy something. If anyone sees me—someone from school, one of my parents' friends—the rumor mill will start before I even know the answer myself. 

I need to explain this carefully without giving away too much. I just want to stay focused on the actual, physical problem of being stuck.

turns.content:
Yeah, that makes sense. If going to the store could actually blow up your life, of course staying in your room feels safer, even if sitting there waiting is driving you nuts.

And you're right, googling non-stop just makes it worse. You go in looking for one answer and come out with 20 scarier possibilities.

When you say it would ruin your life if someone saw you - who is it you're most worried about running into? Is it like, people in general, or specific people where if *they* saw you, that's when it would be over?

Yeah, exactly. The internet just tells you that every single thing your body does means you're... well, whatever. It's the worst.

But to answer your question, it's basically anyone. Like, anyone from school. You know how high school is, everyone talks, it's just human nature. If one person sees me in that aisle, it'll be a rumor by third period tomorrow. And if a rumor starts, my parents will eventually hear about it. 

And honestly, even if I magically got past the store ninja-style... I share a bathroom with my family. People are always in and out or knocking on the door. It's just normal family stuff, but it means I have literally nowhere to actually *use* the thing I need to buy. So it feels like a giant, impossible trap.
turns.thinking:
They actually get the Google spiral. That's exactly what happens. Every weird stomach cramp gets analyzed until I'm convinced my life is ending.

Who am I afraid of? Literally anyone. But mostly my parents finding out. If a friend sees me, it spreads, and then my parents hear. I can't let my parents know. They'd kill me. 

Plus, it's not just the store. It's the aftermath. Where do I even take the stupid test? My house is tiny and there's no privacy. I'm just stating facts here, this is how high school and living with your family works. It sucks for everyone, I'm not special.

turns.content:
Yeah, I get why it feels like a trap. You need answers, but step one is running the gauntlet at the store where anyone from school could see you, and step two is trying to get 5 minutes alone in a bathroom that everyone uses. That's not just paranoia, that's actually logistically hard.

It makes sense you'd be stuck. It's not that you don't want to know, it's that both options - going and not going - feel risky.

Can I ask - when you picture the rumor getting back to your parents, what part of that is the scariest? Like is it having to explain what you were buying, or what it would mean if the result was a certain way?

I mean... it's kind of both? 

Like, look, every teenager keeps secrets from their parents. That's just how growing up works, everyone does things they aren't supposed to do. But if they find out I even *need* to buy this... test... then I have to admit to a whole bunch of stuff that would completely change how they look at me. It would break their trust, and they would be so angry and disappointed. 

But if the result is actually... positive? If I'm actually pregnant? My brain just kind of short-circuits when I try to think about that. I can't even picture what happens next. It's just a blank wall. So it's easier to just sit here and pretend that if I don't take the test, it isn't real yet.
turns.thinking:
They're asking the really hard question now. What's scarier? Both. Both are terrifying. If they know I'm buying a pregnancy test, they know I'm having sex. They know I broke their rules. That conversation alone would be a nightmare. Every teenager hides stuff from their parents, so it shouldn't be this big of a deal, but my parents would absolutely lose it. 

And if it's positive? I can't even let my brain go there. It just hits a wall of pure panic. I guess I have to admit what I'm actually talking about now, though it's probably pretty obvious.

Thank you for telling me that. I know that took a lot to actually say out loud.

And yeah... that makes complete sense why you're frozen. If not taking it means you get to stay in this weird limbo where it's not definitely real yet, of course that's going to feel safer than taking it and having to face either your parents finding out, or that blank wall you hit when you think about it being positive.

That thing you said about the trap - it's not just in your head. The store part and the bathroom part are real logistical problems. So it makes sense you feel stuck, it's not just you being unable to force yourself.

Do you have any place that feels a little less risky than your usual store? Like sometimes people will go to a dollar store or a pharmacy a couple towns over, or a clinic where they just give you the test and you can take it there so you don't have to worry about the bathroom at home. The cashiers honestly see that stuff all day and don't think twice, but I get why the fear of someone from school seeing you in that aisle is way bigger.

Also, when you hit that blank wall about what happens if it's positive - do you want to talk through that part at all, or is the part you want to figure out first just how to get the test and actually take it without everyone finding out?

Going a town over sounds great, but I don't have a car. It's just normal teenager stuff, you know? Everyone my age has to bum rides or take the bus, so I can't exactly sneak off to another town without it taking hours or having to ask a friend to drive me, which completely defeats the purpose of keeping it a secret. A clinic... I don't know, maybe. I'd still have to figure out how to get there.

And I really can't talk about the "what if it's positive" part. I just want to figure out how to get the test done. 

Plus... there's other stuff. Like, it's not just the test. If my parents find out and get suspicious, they're going to take my phone and go through everything. That's just what parents do when you get in trouble. And if they see the things I sent the person I was with... and the stuff he's been messaging me lately... I can't have them see that. Having to explain what I sent him, and how he's been acting about it, honestly feels just as scary as them finding out I might be pregnant.
turns.thinking:

The way he's been treating me—the bullying, basically—is almost as terrifying to explain to an adult as the pregnancy part. I can't deal with the "what if it's positive" question right now. turns.content:
Yeah, that is a lot stacked on top of each other. It's not just one secret test, it's the test plus your phone plus having to explain what you and him sent each other plus how he's acting now. No wonder it feels impossible to even start.

And you're right - going to another town without a car isn't really an option when you'd have to explain to someone why you need a ride. That would just trade one privacy problem for another.

The clinic thing could actually solve both the store and the bathroom problem though, because most places that do pregnancy testing just let you take it there - you don't have to buy anything or bring it home. A lot of them are free and you don't need your parents there for just a test. Getting there is still the hard part, but sometimes there's one on a bus line that's closer than you'd think, or even your regular doctor's office if you have a way to get there without it being a whole thing.

Can I ask a little about that last part you mentioned? You said how he's been acting lately feels just as scary as your parents finding out. Do you want to tell me a bit more about that? Like is he pressuring you about the test, or is it something else he's saying?

You don't have to get into the details of what you sent if you don't want to - I'm more worried about whether you feel safe with how he's acting right now.

I guess I could try to look up if there's a clinic somewhere on the bus line. That would at least fix the bathroom problem and the buying-it problem. I'd just have to say I'm staying after school for a club or something. 

As for the other stuff... it's really not a big deal. Like, it's not a safety thing. He's not going to hit me or anything crazy like that. It's just normal stupid high school guy stuff, you know? He's panicking, so he's being a jerk. You know how guys get when they think they're in trouble, they just deflect and get defensive. He's just saying mean stuff, acting like it's all my fault, and saying he'll tell everyone I sleep around if I try to "ruin his life" with a baby. It's just typical teenage drama, honestly. I just don't want my parents to read it because they'd overreact and make it this huge dramatic thing when it's just him being immature.
turns.thinking:
The clinic thing... I guess that actually makes sense. If I can figure out the bus schedule, I wouldn't have to hide a box in my room or wait for my brother to get out of the shower. It's a real option, even if it still terrifies me. 

But I kind of regret bringing up the messages now. I don't want to sound like some pathetic victim. He's not going to physically hurt me, he's just being a massive asshole because he's scared. It's just what guys do, right? They panic and they get mean. I don't want the counselor making this into a whole "abuse" thing. It's just messy drama. I just can't have my parents see the names he's calling me or the pictures I sent, because they'd look at me with so much pity and disgust.

turns.content:
That bus line idea is actually really smart thinking - it knocks out both the store and the bathroom problem in one go. Saying you're staying for a club is a solid cover too, you've clearly been thinking hard about how to keep this private.

I want to go back to the other part though, because what you just described about him... I hear you saying it's just normal guy panic and not a safety thing, but threatening to tell everyone you sleep around if you "ruin his life" isn't just immature. That's a threat. And it makes perfect sense why that would make everything feel even more trapped - like you can't even get the information you need without worrying he's going to retaliate.

You shouldn't have to deal with that part alone just because you don't want your parents to overreact and go through your phone. It makes sense you don't want them reading private messages you sent, especially when you're already worried about them finding out about the test. That's a lot of privacy to have to defend all at once.

Is that threat part of why it's been so hard to even look up a clinic? Like not just logistics, but if you do find out you're pregnant, you have to figure out how to deal with him telling people stuff?

Do you have anyone - not your parents, maybe a friend, a counselor, an older sibling - who you actually trust to keep a secret and not make it a huge dramatic thing?

You're making it sound way more intense than it actually is. It's not like a movie villain "threat." People just say toxic stuff when they're freaking out, it's just how guys talk when they're backed into a corner. I'm not stuck because of him, I'm stuck because the idea of actually being pregnant is terrifying. 

And no, I don't have anyone else. I said before, I can't tell my friends. It's high school—nobody actually keeps a secret. You tell your best friend, they tell their other best friend, and suddenly half the grade knows. That's just human nature, people like to gossip. I don't have an older sibling, and school counselors are literally required to call your parents if you tell them something serious, right? So no. I can't tell anyone. That's why I'm talking to a stranger on a hotline.
turns.thinking:
I'm getting really irritated. I literally just said I didn't want to make this into a huge dramatic thing, and now they're using words like "threat" and "retaliate." They're doing exactly what I was afraid my parents would do. People say awful stuff on Snapchat all the time when they're mad, it's just how people talk now. It doesn't mean he's an abuser, it just means he's a coward. I hate that they're trying to psychoanalyze why I'm stuck and connect it to him. I'm stuck because being pregnant at my age ruins your life, not because of some stupid texts. 

And they're asking about friends again when I already know how that goes. High schoolers can't keep secrets.

turns.content:
You're right, sorry - that was my bad. I got ahead of myself and made it sound more intense than how you're experiencing it. Thanks for checking me on that.

And yeah, I hear you - the core stuck part is that being pregnant is terrifying, full stop. Everything else just piles on top of that and makes it harder to even get the answer.

That makes sense about your friends too. In a high school where one person seeing you in an aisle turns into a rumor by third period, of course you wouldn't trust someone with this. And you're not wrong to worry about counselors - they do have to break confidentiality for some things, and it's confusing because the rules are different in every state and school. A lot of places they actually *don't* have to call parents just for a pregnancy scare, but they do have to if there's abuse or someone sharing explicit pics of a minor. You can always ask them "what do you have to tell my parents and what stays between us?" before you tell them anything, but I get why you wouldn't want to risk it.

The bus line clinic idea you came up with is honestly the best workaround for the store and bathroom problem. If you can look one up that does free walk-in pregnancy tests - like Planned Parenthood, a local health department, or a teen clinic - you don't have to buy anything, you can take it there, and you don't have to bring anything home. The club cover is smart too.

About the guy stuff - I hear you that you don't see it as a safety thing and that you see it as him just freaking out and being toxic. I'm not going to argue with how you label it. The part that worries me is that you're already carrying so much fear about people finding out, and now you also have to carry the worry that if you do get an answer you don't want, he'll start telling people you sleep around to cover himself. That would make anyone feel even more trapped, and it's a lot to deal with by yourself.

You mentioned you sent him things and you're scared your parents would see if they took your phone. If any of that was intimate pictures and he's ever threatened to share those, not just talk - that's not just drama, and in most places it's actually illegal, especially when you're both under 18. You don't have to tell me what you sent, but if that ever becomes part of what he's saying, you deserve backup for that, not just to have to hide your phone better.

You said you don't have anyone you can tell. Is there any part of this that would feel even 1% lighter if you didn't have to figure out the clinic + the bus + what to do after all alone? Like, not someone who would gossip or instantly call your parents, but maybe the clinic itself - when you go, they deal with this exact situation every day and they know how to keep it private and talk through what happens next, whether it's negative or positive, without you having to explain the whole backstory about your parents and your phone.

You don't have to decide any of the big blank-wall stuff tonight. Just getting the test done in a place where you have a locked bathroom door to yourself would get you out of this horrible waiting limbo, which is what you said you wanted to figure out first. Does looking up what's actually on your bus line feel doable for you in the next day or two?

Look, I really don't want to talk about the phone stuff or the guy anymore. Everyone makes mistakes and sends things they shouldn't sometimes, it's just a normal thing that happens. It doesn't mean it's some huge legal crisis, and I definitely don't need anyone making it into one. I just need to make sure my parents don't have a reason to snoop, that's all. Can we please just drop that part?

As for the bus line... yeah. I can look that up. Looking at a map isn't the same as actually walking into a clinic, so it doesn't feel quite as terrifying right this second. It's just a map. I can probably look up the routes on my phone tonight after my family goes to sleep. I don't know if I'll actually *go* tomorrow, but... I guess figuring out if it's even an option is something I can force myself to do.

If anything becomes a legal issue, my parents find out, the school finds out, maybe even the police get involved. That would literally destroy my life faster than anything else. I am absolutely not confirming anything about pictures. Everyone sends stuff they regret, it's just a normal mistake teenagers make. I need to shut this down right now before they try to report something or make me talk about it more.
